blocking.title: New guide section says the profile name 'comes from a filename' and uses a profile name aelix rejects as its example
blocking.detail: docs/guides/agent-profiles.md, in the new section 'What you see while a child runs' (the bundled copy is identical). It says 'the profile name too, since it comes from a filename' and 'A profile named `리뷰　어` shows as `리뷰 어`'. Both are false for aelix. SubagentProgress.profile is resolved.name, which is the profile's `name:` field. parse_profile requires that field to match ^[a-z0-9-]+$ with at most 64 characters, and the same guide's key table says 'This field, not the filename'. So aelix's own runtime cannot produce that example; the only field that can carry an NBSP, ESC or excess width is the child's tool name. The same premise appears in ADR-0199 section (l) ('`profile` a filename', and 'a profile name that relies on a no-break space to read right is the one visible cost') and in the message's WHY section ('profile a filename'). Fix: base the example on a tool name. State that the profile is the profile's validated name field, so only another SubagentRuntime could hand over a dirty one, and name the real visible cost (a tool name).
blocking.evidence: parse_profile on 'name: "리뷰　어"' gives profile None, with diagnostic error 'name contains invalid characters (must be lowercase a-z, 0-9, hyphens only)'. Real CLI (isolated agent dir holding agents/review.md with that name, fake key): 'aelix --agent "리뷰　어" -p hi' prints 'Error: unknown agent profile ...; available: explorer, general-purpose'. Sources: profile.py:48-50 and 431-450, runtime.py:593 and 657, guide table row `name`. Kit: .omc/probes/178-live/r2verify/results.txt

nonblocking.title: The sanitised-half wording overclaims when a deleted control sits next to whitespace
nonblocking.detail: The ADR, docstrings, CHANGELOG and guide say every whitespace run becomes ONE U+0020 and leading and trailing whitespace goes. _flatten collapses whitespace first and deletes controls afterwards, so a deleted steering character can leave a double, leading or trailing space. The output stays safe; only the description is too strong. Fix by stripping before collapsing, or by saying it.
nonblocking.evidence: probes/probe_r2.out (fix tree): 'a \x1b b' prints 'a  b'; '\x1b read' prints ' read' (card '·  read ·'); 'read \x07' prints 'read '; '\x01 \x02' keeps a one-space tool term ('·   ·'), so 'only controls drops the term' holds only for controls with no space.

nonblocking.title: The definition of 'clean' omits the zero-width backstop (4 code points per cell)
nonblocking.detail: _flatten clips anything longer than limit*_ZERO_WIDTH_SLACK code points (312 at 78 cells), even when it is narrower than 78 cells. A field that meets all three of the ADR's clauses can therefore still come out with an ellipsis, so the identity half is false for it. Only pathological input reaches this.
